# Results — Study 759 (Redbook-Retail)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The consumer-nowcasting folklore
— **accelerating Redbook same-store retail sales lead retail stocks** — tested on the monthly
**Redbook year-over-year same-store** tape (a hardcoded, clearly-labelled **approximate
reconstruction**, since the weekly Redbook Index is proprietary and off FRED) against month-end
**XRT** (SPDR S&P Retail ETF, yfinance, total-return adjusted). We split forward 1/3/6/12-month
XRT returns into months when Redbook momentum is **accelerating** vs **decelerating**, compare
each to the unconditional base rate, and add a Welch *t*, a placebo null, a lead/lag scan, a
retail-vs-market relative test, a level-regime split and a tradable timing overlay. Offline &
deterministic; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Redbook tape | Johnson Redbook same-store sales, YoY (%); **hardcoded monthly LABELLED PROXY** (proprietary series, off FRED) — faithful in shape, approximate in level |
| Equity tape | yfinance daily **XRT** (+**SPY** for the relative test) adjusted close (total-return adjusted), month-end sampled |
| Window | 2006-06-30 → 2026-06-30 (**241** months; **20.0** years — XRT's whole listed life) |
| Signal | Redbook momentum = YoY level vs **3 months** prior; **ACCELERATING** when > 0 |
| Entry / costs | **1-month execution lag** (act on the next month-end close); 10 bps one-way per switch on the overlay |

> **Proxy caveat (named on the Signal axis).** The weekly Redbook Index is a paid, proprietary
> feed, so the series here is a hardcoded monthly **approximate reconstruction** of the YoY
> same-store number — public in *shape* (the 2008–09 slide into **negative** growth, the strong
> 2018–19 run, the COVID-2020 collapse, the 2021–22 double-digit reopening/inflation surge to a
> ~**+16.8%** peak in Nov 2021, the 2023 deceleration) but **not the licensed tape** and
> approximate in monthly level. It is a **labelled proxy**, never a real-tape banner. The
> 2021–22 surge was largely **nominal inflation** — a fact the verdict leans on, not around.

## The signal — forward XRT returns when Redbook is ACCELERATING vs the base rate (absolute)

1-month execution lag; the base column is *all* months. The believers say ACCELERATING Redbook
should lift the forward return; Welch *t* compares the ACCEL-set mean to the unconditional mean
(a real nowcast ⇒ **significantly positive** *t*). The placebo *p* is the share of 20,000 random
same-size month draws whose mean forward return is **at least** the ACCEL set's (as bullish or
more).

| horizon | n accel | accel mean | decel mean | base mean | accel up-rate | base up-rate | Welch *t* | placebo *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1-month  | 105 | **+1.04%** | +1.02% | +1.03% | 56% | 56% | **+0.01** | 0.494 |
| 3-month  | 104 | **+4.01%** | +2.33% | +3.07% | 66% | 61% | **+0.63** | 0.222 |
| 6-month  | 101 | **+9.13%** | +4.07% | +6.26% | 70% | 62% | **+1.21** | 0.076 |
| 12-month | 99 | **+14.07%** | +12.64% | +13.26% | 73% | 65% | **+0.24** | 0.398 |

Read it carefully. The direction is *right* only at 3–6 months (accel above base), and even the
best case — **6-month, +9.1% vs +6.3%** — is a Welch **t = +1.21**, well short of the bar. At
**1 month it's a dead tie** (+1.04% vs +1.03%) and at **12 months** almost nothing (+14.1% vs
+13.3%). A small, horizon-specific bump inside the noise — not a signal.

## Retail-vs-market — does Redbook predict XRT *beating* SPY?

The sharper "leads retail *stocks*" test: repeat the split on XRT-minus-SPY forward returns.

| horizon | n accel | accel mean (XRT−SPY) | base mean | Welch *t* | placebo *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1-month  | 105 | **−0.39%** | +0.04% | **−0.82** | 0.819 |
| 3-month  | 104 | +0.21% | +0.09% | +0.11 | 0.430 |
| 6-month  | 101 | +1.69% | +0.31% | **+0.79** | 0.156 |
| 12-month | 99 | **+0.16%** | +1.17% | **−0.40** | 0.650 |

The tiny absolute 6-month tilt is **mostly market beta**: on a retail-*minus*-market basis it's
+1.7% at *t* = +0.79 (insignificant), and it turns **negative** at 1 and 12 months. Redbook does
**not** pick retail over the broad market.

## The decisive test — does the Redbook uptick *lead* the stocks?

The whole pitch is **"nowcast."** So we scan the correlation of Redbook momentum at *t* against
the XRT return over `[t+L, t+L+1]`. A genuine nowcast would show its strongest *positive*
correlation at a **positive** lead (Redbook moves first, the stocks follow).

| lead *L* (months) | −4 | −3 | −2 | −1 | 0 | +1 | +3 | +6 |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| corr(Redbook-mom, fwd XRT) | +0.31 | **+0.33** | +0.27 | +0.06 | +0.02 | −0.04 | +0.05 | −0.11 |

The strongest positive correlation sits at **L = −3** — Redbook momentum is most associated with
the retail move *three months in its **past***. At positive leads (Redbook supposedly leading)
the correlation is near **zero or negative**. Redbook isn't a nowcast; the uptick is a
**coincident-to-lagging** echo of a sector the market already repriced. That is the core of the
"leads retail? — Not supported" stamp.

## Level regime — the only significant result points the WRONG way

Split on the *level* (not the acceleration): forward XRT returns in STRONG (Redbook YoY above the
full-sample median) vs WEAK same-store months.

| horizon | strong mean | weak mean | spread | Welch *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1-month  | +0.36% (n=113) | +1.63% (n=126) | **−1.26%** | −1.37 |
| 12-month | +7.82% (n=102) | +17.66% (n=126) | **−9.84%** | **−2.28** |

Strong nominal same-store months precede **weaker** forward returns — a 9.8-point 12-month gap
the *wrong way*, at *t* = −2.28 (significant). This is the 2021–22 tell: peak nominal same-store
growth was peak inflation, and XRT fell afterward. The lore's "own retail when the consumer is
strong" is, if anything, mildly contrarian.

## Tradability — the "own XRT when Redbook is accelerating" overlay

Hold XRT when Redbook is accelerating, sit in cash when decelerating (one-month lag; 10 bps per
switch, turnover one-way × NAV). Sharpe is excess-of-zero (the cash leg earns 0 here — a
conservative, labelled simplification).

| book | ann. mean | ann. Sharpe | switches | $1 → |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| buy-and-hold XRT | **+12.1%** | **0.49** | — | **$6.06** |
| overlay, gross | +8.6% | 0.52 | 74 | — |
| overlay, net @ 10 bps | **+8.2%** | **0.50** | 74 | **$4.01** |

The overlay **underperforms buy-and-hold** on return (**+8.2% vs +12.1%**/yr; $1 → **$4.01 vs
$6.06** over 20 years). Its Sharpe is a near-tie (0.50 vs 0.49) — you buy *volatility reduction*
by sitting out half the time, but **no extra reward**. Acting on the signal subtracts return.

## Robustness — window, smoothing, relative, ex-COVID (6-month)

| variation | n accel | accel 6m mean | Welch *t* | placebo *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| momentum **k = 1** | 111 | +7.9% | +0.72 | 0.199 |
| momentum **k = 3** (base) | 101 | +9.1% | **+1.21** | 0.076 |
| momentum **k = 6** | 118 | +6.5% | +0.12 | 0.441 |
| **smoothed** (3-mo) | 122 | +7.3% | +0.49 | 0.279 |
| **relative** (XRT−SPY) | 101 | +1.7% | +0.79 | 0.156 |
| **drop 2020–2022H1** (ex-COVID) | 87 | +9.0% | +1.22 | 0.097 |

The bump is a single fragile artefact: highest at **k = 3** (*t* = +1.21) and collapsing under
every other choice (k = 6 → +0.12; smoothed → +0.49; relative → +0.79). Even dropping the entire
COVID/inflation window leaves it at *t* = +1.22 — **no specification clears t = 2.**

## Synthetic positive control — the engine is faithful

A deterministic monthly Redbook + XRT-like series with a *planted* link (accelerating momentum at
*t* lifts the *t+1* return by `edge`). The detector + inference must recover a planted edge and
must **not** manufacture significance when the true edge is zero.

| planted edge (monthly) | n accel | accel 1m mean | base 1m mean | Welch *t* | placebo *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **0.00** (no link) | 183 | +1.88% | +1.50% | **+0.72** | 0.194 |
| **+0.05** (large link) | 183 | +6.25% | +4.10% | **+3.66** | 0.000 |

With **no** planted link the test sits at *t* = +0.72 (no false positive, p = 0.19); a large
planted link drives *t* to **+3.66**. The machinery is unbiased — so the real-tape *t* of ~+1.2
(at its best) is exactly what an *absent-or-tiny* Redbook→returns edge looks like through this
keyhole.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The best horizon (6-month) tilt is **+9.1% vs +6.3%** at Welch **t = +1.21**
  (placebo *p* = 0.08) — it **fails the *t* ≥ 2 bar**, is a dead tie at 1 month and near-nothing
  at 12, is fragile to every specification choice, and is **market beta** (retail-vs-market
  relative excess *t* = +0.79 at 6m, negative at 1m/12m). Indistinguishable from noise.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The "own retail when Redbook accelerates" overlay **underperforms
  buy-and-hold** (**+8.2% vs +12.1%**/yr; $1 → **$4.01 vs $6.06**). It buys volatility reduction,
  not reward — acting on the signal *destroys* return. Nothing to allocate to.
- **Leads retail? — NOT SUPPORTED.** The lead/lag scan puts the strongest positive correlation at
  **L = −3** (Redbook momentum *lagging* XRT by a quarter, ρ = +0.33); at positive leads it's
  ~zero. Redbook is a **coincident-to-lagging** echo, not a leader — and the only *significant*
  level-regime result (*t* = −2.28) runs **against** the folklore, the fingerprint of a nominal,
  inflation-contaminated series. The whole appeal — *nowcast* — is the part the data rejects.
